intro.title: Lifting State Up
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple temperature converter app with two input fields: one for Celsius and one for Fahrenheit. You will learn the core React concept of 'Lifting State Up', which means managing shared state in a common parent component to keep multiple child components in sync. The main technologies involved are React functional components, TypeScript for type safety, and the useState hook to manage state. By the end, you'll understand how to pass state and update functions as props to create a controlled, interactive form.
intro.usecase: Lifting state up is essential when multiple UI components need to share and synchronize data. In real applications, you'll use this pattern for dashboard widgets that display the same metrics, e-commerce filters that update product listings, or form sections that validate together. For example, when a user selects a date range in one panel, other charts and tables across the dashboard must reflect that same timeframe. This pattern ensures consistency across complex interfaces where independent components must react to shared data changes.
